questions.q: A song plays over a driving montage like ordinary score. Then the driver switches it off mid-chorus. What has the film just done?
choices: Used an L-cut to carry sound into the next scene
Revealed the music was diegetic all along, pulling us into the characters' present moment
Used Mickey-Mousing to match the action
questions.explain: The music crosses from apparent score into the story world: it was on the car radio, so the montage becomes a scene in real time.

questions.q: Which of these is non-diegetic sound?
choices: A band playing in the corner of the bar
A gunshot offscreen that the characters turn toward
An orchestral score swelling as the lovers kiss
A radio playing in the kitchen
questions.explain: The characters can't hear the score; only the audience can. Offscreen sound can still be diegetic.

questions.q: An editor lets the sound of a train start a few seconds before we cut to the station. What is this?
questions.explain: In a J-cut the next scene's sound arrives before its picture, pulling attention forward.

questions.q: A villain is only a voice on the phone for most of a thriller, seemingly able to see everything the hero does. When we finally see him, he seems smaller. Which idea explains this?
choices: The acousmêtre and its de-acousmatization, from Michel Chion
questions.explain: Chion's acousmêtre is a heard-but-unseen character with apparent powers that vanish when the body is shown.

questions.q: A foley artist punches a cabbage, and the audience hears a fist hitting a face. What has Chion named this welding of sound and image?
questions.explain: Synchresis is the mind's habit of fusing a sound and image that happen at the same moment.

questions.q: During a battle, the noise suddenly turns muffled and distant, with a ringing tone, as the hero is stunned. What technique is this?
questions.explain: We hear the scene through the character's damaged ears, as in Saving Private Ryan's Omaha Beach landing.

questions.q: Who is widely described as the first person credited as a film's "sound designer"?
questions.explain: Murch's credit on Apocalypse Now is usually cited as the first; Chion is a theorist, Herrmann and Williams composers.

ideas: Whether the characters can hear a sound changes whether it acts as evidence or as commentary.
A voice heard but never seen seems all-powerful until the body it belongs to is shown.
Letting one scene's sound start before its picture, or linger after it, binds two scenes together.
Sound gives an image meaning so smoothly that we believe the meaning was in the picture all along.
